children.text: Permanent magnets

Uniformly magnetized permanent magnets have magnetization J=1.5 T/μ0, where μ0=\(4\pi\times10^{-7}\) SI. A uniformly magnetized body has moment m=JV. Outside a spherical magnet its field is the point-dipole field \(\mathbf B=\mu_0(2\mathbf m_\parallel-\mathbf m_\perp)/(4\pi r^3)\). A uniformly magnetized cylinder can be represented by a surface current along its curved side. In A1-A3 the cylinders have diameter d=2.0 cm and height h=2.0 mm, with magnetization along their axes. In A4-A5 spherical magnets have diameter δ=5.0 mm and material density 7500 kg/m³. For high-permeability bodies in B, take μ≫μ0 and retain finite closed magnetic flux paths. In C use only nearest-neighbour dipole interactions for equal spheres in a plane. An illustrative source sketch accompanies each geometric construction.

statement.text:

Outside a spherical magnet its field is the point-dipole field \(\mathbf B=\mu_0(2\mathbf m_\parallel-\mathbf m_\perp)/(4\pi r^3)\). In A4-A5 spherical magnets have diameter δ=5.0 mm and material density 7500 kg/m³. For high-permeability bodies in B, take μ≫μ0 and retain finite closed magnetic flux paths. In C use only nearest-neighbour dipole interactions for equal spheres in a plane. An illustrative source sketch accompanies each geometric construction.

children.text: Permanent magnets
a.1. Distant coaxial magnets
Each moment is \(m=J\pi d^2h/4=0.75\,\mathrm{A\,m^2}\). Differentiate the axial dipole interaction energy to obtain \(F=3\mu_0m^2/(2\pi L^4)=2.11\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm N\).
a.2. Equivalent circulating current
Bound surface current density is J, so the total circulating current across cylinder height is \(I=Jh\simeq2.39\times10^3\,\mathrm A\).
a.3. Closely spaced cylinders

Locally the side currents are parallel wires separated by L. Integrate the force per length μ0I²/(2πL) around circumference πd: \(F\simeq\mu_0I^2d/(2L)\simeq14\,\mathrm N\). This neglects curvature and finite height.
a.4. Hanging sphere chain

For one sphere m=Jπδ³/6 and mass M=ρπδ³/6. The top sphere supports the lower chain through \(F=3\mu_0m^2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n^{-4}/(2\pi\delta^4)=\mu_0m^2\pi^3/(60\delta^4)\). Equate to NMg, giving roughly 1320 spheres and length 6.6 m. This is an ideal straight-chain estimate ignoring mechanical instability.
a.5. Field near a long chain end

The moments per unit length m/δ form a thin solenoid. Away from its remote end the near endpoint acts as a magnetic pole of strength m/δ. Thus \[B=\frac{\mu_0m}{4\pi\delta r^2}=\frac{\mu_0J\delta^2}{24r^2},\] independent of θ. Field is radial from O, outward for a north endpoint and inward for a south endpoint. The conditions permit a continuum approximation and neglect of the far endpoint.
b.1. Field lines at a permeable plate

Normal B and tangential H are continuous. If α and β are the angles to the surface normal inside and outside the plate, \(\tan\alpha=(\mu/\mu_0)\tan\beta\). For μ≫μ0 the external line meets the surface almost normally. Each magnetic line must close. Lines entering the plate return through it and emerge elsewhere, possibly very far away. They must not terminate in the plate or leave through its distant lower face in the depicted thick-plate approximation. The source statement refers to three points on a separate answer sheet, not retained with its PDF. Here those path families are stated explicitly, and the source worked sketch is supplied in the solution.

nodes.alt: Original worked field-line paths around the spherical magnet and through the high-permeability plate.

children.text: b.2. Contact force and orientation

An image magnet mirrored in the plane has parallel normal moment, with centre separation δ. Either polarity normal to the plate is a stable orientation. The attractive force is \(F=3\mu_0m^2/(2\pi\delta^4)\simeq5.9\,\mathrm N\).
b.3. Magnet between circular plates

Flux conservation gives B1d²=B2(D²−d²), so B1=3B2. Ampère circulation with side current Jh gives B1+B2=μ0J. Hence B1=3μ0J/4=1.125 T and opposite return field has magnitude B2=μ0J/4=0.375 T. Maxwell pressure integrated over the inner disc and outer annulus gives \[F=\frac\pi{8\mu_0}[d^2B_1^2+(D^2-d^2)B_2^2]=\frac{3\pi\mu_0J^2d^2}{32}\simeq210\,\mathrm N.\] Field energy alone at fixed permanent magnetization misses the magnet's interaction energy and can give a wrong force sign.
c.1. Square lattice

One stable pattern has parallel moments along each horizontal row and opposite moments in adjacent rows. The nearest-neighbour field at a sphere is \(B=3\mu_0m/(2\pi\delta^3)\), aligned with its moment. Removing the sphere breaks its interactions and costs \(W=mB=3\mu_0m^2/(2\pi\delta^3)\simeq29\,\mathrm{mJ}\). Do not divide this single-removal energy by two. The source also accepts an appropriate vortex-like stable pattern, so the sketch is self-reviewed.
c.2. Triangular lattice

A stable arrangement has all moments parallel to one lattice direction. Sum the six dipole fields, whose transverse components cancel, to get \(B=3\mu_0m/(4\pi\delta^3)\). The removal energy is \(W=3\mu_0m^2/(4\pi\delta^3)\simeq15\,\mathrm{mJ}\).
